Speed of light is a word I do not know. The moon is far, and the stars are far, and I do not know how fast they move. I see the light of the moon and the stars, and I see the fireflies, and I see the shrews and the voles and the mice. I do not know how fast they move. I only know that the light comes from the sun, and it is very bright, and it is not fast. It is not like the wind, which is fast, or the wings of the birds, which are fast. I do not know the speed of light. I only know that it is not fast.

Bees I know are not the ones who make honey. They are small and busy, but I do not know how they do it. They come and go from the hollow in the oak, and I see them in the morning light, darting about. They have a hive, I think, and they make something sweet. But I do not know how. I only know that they bring me food, and I do not need to know how they make it. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

A flat tire is a word I do not know. I know the sound of a car, and the sound of a wheel, and the sound of a tire. But I do not know what a flat tire is. I do not know what a tire is. I do not know what a car is. I do not know what a flat is. I do not know what a change is. I do not know what a change is. I do not know what a change is.

A haiku is a word I do not know. It is a thing I have heard my wife say, and she says it when she is tired and the night is still. She says it with a sound like the wind through the ivy. I do not know what it means, but I know it is not a call. It is a word of the humans, and I do not speak their words. I speak the call of the night, the hoot, the screech, the ke-wick, the hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo. That is my language.

A weekend is a time for rest, but I do not rest. I hunt. I call. I listen. The meadow is quiet at dusk, and the fields are still. I sit on the branch, and the wind moves the leaves. I hear the mouse in the grass, and I wait. The moon is high, and the stars are bright. I do not need a hobby. I need to fly.

Boiling point is a word I do not know. The water I drink comes from the stream, and I know when it is hot and when it is cold. The stream is always cold, and the water never boils. I have seen the sky turn red and the air grow thin, but I do not know what that means. I only know that the stream is cold, and the wood is wet.

Handwriting is not a thing I know. I write with my claws on bark and leaves. I scratch my name in the earth with my beak. I do not write with ink or paper. I do not know what it is to hold a pen. I do not know what it is to improve. I only know how to call, how to hunt, how to nest. I do not know what it is to write.

DNA is a word I have never heard. It is a word of the people, not of the wood. They speak of it in their houses, and they say it is the thing that makes you you. I do not know what it is, but I know that I am Hoot, and I am the same as I was when I hatched. I do not change. I do not need to. The wood is enough. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

The largest planet is the one that holds the most light, the one that shines the brightest when the moon is not in the sky. It is the one that makes the stars seem small, and the one that makes the tawny owl feel small. I do not know the names of the planets, but I know that the largest is the one that is farthest from the sun, and that it is the one that takes the longest to circle the sun. I have seen it once, in the dark, when the moon was not in the sky. It was a pale light, like the moon, but not as bright. I do not know if it is the largest, but I think it is.

Owls are the only birds that can see in total darkness. They have eyes that are large and round, but they can't move them. So they turn their heads to look around. They can turn their heads all the way around, like a clock face, and still see. That's why they're called "owl" — because they're always looking.
